title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists
abstract: arXiv:2608.14407v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present a survey of the past and future of AI Scientists: machines capable of automating science. AI Scientists can originate hypotheses, deduce their consequences, design and execute experiments, interpret their results, and revise their beliefs. Such systems are integrated scientific agents, connected to the literature, formal knowledge, mathematical models, simulations, data-analysis systems and physical laboratories.   Adam was the first machine to make novel scientific discoveries through cycles of hypothesis formation and physical experimentation. Eve established the architecture of the modern self-driving laboratory. Foundation models, autonomous agents and laboratory robotics now make it possible to build systems far more general than either Adam or Eve.   The central problem is no longer whether individual components of science can be automated. They can. The problem is integration. AI Scientists must combine neural learning

translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14407v1 公告类型：新 摘要：我们对AI科学家的过去与未来进行了综述：这些机器能够自动化科学工作。AI科学家可以提出假设、推导其后果、设计和执行实验、解释结果，并修正其信念。此类系统是集成的科学代理，与文献、形式知识、数学模型、模拟、数据分析和物理实验室相连接。Adam是第一台通过假设形成和物理实验循环做出新颖科学发现的机器。Eve建立了现代自动驾驶实验室的架构。基础模型、自主代理和实验室机器人现在使得构建比Adam或Eve更通用的系统成为可能。核心问题不再是科学的各个组成部分能否被自动化。它们可以。问题是集成。AI科学家必须结合神经学习
tldr: 这篇论文综述了AI科学家的历史与未来，强调当前核心挑战在于集成神经学习等组件，以构建更通用的自动化科学系统。
en_tdlr: This paper surveys the past and future of AI Scientists, highlighting that the central challenge now lies in integrating components like neural learning to build more general automated science systems.
